date_note: Date of Macromill's own notice; it confirmed the access on 29 Oct. ScanNetSecurity reported it on 18 Nov.
title: Macromill monitor site: information of 317 monitors viewed in unauthorized access, point exchange suspended
summary: Macromill said on 12 November that unauthorized third-party access to part of its monitor site's systems was confirmed on 29 October. Basic and attribute information of 317 monitors was viewed, and for 82 of them the registered bank account details too. It says there were attempts to change email addresses or exchange points on some accounts, but no completed unauthorized exchange or login is confirmed. Point exchange is suspended.
plain: Macromill says someone got into part of its survey-panel site and viewed data of 317 members; point exchange is paused.
exec: A market-research panel site says 317 members' data was viewed, 82 with bank details; no completed fraud is confirmed.
action: Macromill monitors should follow the company's notice, check their registered email address and points, and stay alert to phishing.

sources.name: Macromill monitor site notice, 12 Nov 2026 (apology and notice on leak of personal information and suspension of point exchange)

validation.note: The company's own notice (12 Nov) and ScanNetSecurity (18 Nov) agree on dates and the 317 and 82 figures; neither states a cause.
